clue.text: The business centre of a place like Bangor

definitions.meaning: the commercial heart of an American city is its central business district
Bangor in Northern Ireland lies in County Down, so it is a town of Down

explanation.walkthrough: Bangor here is the Northern Irish one, in County Down; read as two words the answer is a town in Down.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage the central commercial district of a city is called by this name.

clue.text: Guides do it to order

definitions.meaning: to guide is to steer or show the way

explanation.walkthrough: 'Guides' looks like Girl Guides, the youth organisation, but it is the verb: what someone who guides does.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer or show the way is to direct; to give a command is also to direct.

clue.text: Female without make-up gets feller

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the female goes round the other piece

parts.note: a female is a woman

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word make is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to make is to do, as in do a sketch

explanation.surface: A woman who has stopped wearing cosmetics finds herself a boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' reads as cosmetics, but splits in two, and 'up' turns 'make' over. 'Feller' is a man, but also one who fells trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodman cuts down trees for timber, so he is literally one who fells.

clue.text: Homely documents describing the Acts of the Apostles, for example?

definitions.meaning: papers proving ownership of a home

definitions.text: describing the Acts of the Apostles, for example?
definitions.meaning: the book's name is a heading that tells of deeds, a title for deeds

explanation.walkthrough: 'Homely' is not plain or cosy but to do with a home: the papers showing who owns a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal papers recording ownership of property, especially of a house, go by this name.

clue.text: Horse-trader who engages in shady practice?

definitions.meaning: someone given to sharp, scheming dealings, playing on the cartwheel-like spinning of deals

explanation.definitionFit: A wheeler-dealer is a shrewd, scheming operator, the figurative sense of a horse-trader driving hard bargains.

clue.text: One regularly browsing in Blenheim Palace

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of words Blenheim Palace

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps wandering about the rooms of the stately home Blenheim Palace.
explanation.walkthrough: Blenheim Palace is a grand English stately home in Oxfordshire. 'Browsing' suggests a tourist or shopper, but here it is an animal feeding on leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: This African antelope feeds by browsing on leaves and shoots, so it is a regular browser.

clue.text: Bohemian girl removing article from US city

indicators.note: removing signals that one piece is taken out of the city's name

parts.note: Miami is a city in Florida
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A young woman from Bohemia leaves an American city with some item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bohemian' points to Czech Bohemia, but Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's opera La Bohème, set among bohemian artists in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimi is the seamstress heroine of La Bohème, the opera about Parisian bohemians.

clue.text: Colouring matter an Indian copper initially took to

parts.note: the anna was an old Indian coin, minted in copper

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of took is used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An Indian copper coin was used to make a dye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman but is a copper coin: the anna, a sixteenth of a rupee.
explanation.definitionFit: Annatto is an orange-red dye from a tropical seed, used to colour cheese and butter.

clue.text: A man that time's entangled, like Pericles

indicators.note: entangled means one piece is caught up in the middle of the other

parts.note: Ian is a man's name
then means at that time

explanation.surface: Someone from ancient times caught up in a tangle, compared to the statesman Pericles.
explanation.walkthrough: Pericles was the great statesman of ancient Athens; 'entangled' puts the time word inside the man.
explanation.definitionFit: Pericles led Athens in its golden age, so describing someone as like him means a citizen of that city.

clue.text: Group of players lacking time for port

indicators.note: lacking signals that the group's word goes without one piece

parts.note: a trio is a group of three musicians

explanation.surface: A band one member short is out of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' could be wine or the left side of a ship, but it is a harbour city, Rio de Janeiro.
explanation.definitionFit: Rio de Janeiro, usually shortened to Rio, is a great Brazilian seaport.

clue.text: Size of book, the last for a year

parts.note: twelvemo, or duodecimo, is a book size made by folding sheets into twelve leaves
nth means the last in a series, however far it goes

explanation.surface: A book's format chosen last for a whole year.
explanation.walkthrough: TWELVEMO is a printer's term for a small book format. NTH as 'the last' is a crossword stretch on 'the nth', the furthest in a series.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelvemonth is an old word for a full year, twelve months together.

clue.text: Antonio for one left in a fix — it may be this or curtains

definitions.text: it may be this or curtains

parts.note: Antonio is Shakespeare's merchant of Venice, so a Venetian

indicators.note: in signals the letter for left goes inside the word for fix

parts.note: a bind is a tight spot or fix

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean character is in trouble, and it may be the end for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtains' reads as the end for Antonio, but means window coverings, the alternative to slatted blinds.
explanation.definitionFit: A slatted window blind is a way of covering a window, an alternative to hanging curtains.

clue.text: Driver's action arousing strong interest

definitions.meaning: forcing or driving something along, as a driver of cattle does
gripping, hard to look away from

explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' suggests a motorist; here it is anyone who drives or forces something along.
explanation.definitionFit: Forcing someone to act is driving them; a gripping story is also described with this word.

clue.text: Stagger off one's trolley when going backwards

indicators.note: going backwards means the word for crazy is read right to left

parts.note: off one's trolley is British slang for crazy, nuts

explanation.surface: Someone lurches about out of their mind, staggering backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stagger' looks like walking unsteadily, but it is the verb meaning astonish.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger someone is to astound them, the same as to stun.

clue.text: Objective of Evita's introducing herself to Capone: protecting son

indicators.note: protecting means one piece wraps round and shelters the other

parts.note: Eva Perón, known as Evita, introducing herself would say I'm Perón
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
the gangster Al Capone

explanation.surface: A scene in which Eva Perón introduces herself to the gangster Al Capone, shielding her boy.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes inside I'M PERON, then AL follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An objective judgement is impersonal, free of personal feeling or bias.

clue.text: Make beloved's goal the faculty for appreciating music

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
an ear for music is the gift of appreciating it

explanation.surface: Making the loved one's aim an ear for music.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of beloved's is a link, as in 'is': make beloved is the definition, and goal plus ear the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear someone is to make them loved or cherished.

clue.text: Grave old boy finally missed fairground attraction

parts.note: a tomb is a grave

indicators.note: finally missed means the boy's word loses its last letter

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A serious old pupil skipped the fair's attraction in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave old boy' reads as a solemn former pupil, but Grave is a noun here. A tombola is a raffle drawn from a rotating drum, common at British fairs and fêtes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a lottery stall, a regular fixture at fairs and fêtes in Britain.

clue.text: Coast road like the one at Penzance, some say

indicators.note: some say means the word is spoken, giving a sound match

parts.note: Penzance is in Cornwall, so anything there is Cornish

explanation.surface: A seaside road resembling the one at the Cornish town of Penzance.
explanation.walkthrough: Penzance is a town in Cornwall, the far south-western county of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A corniche is a road cut along a cliff or coast, like the famous ones on the Riviera.

clue.text: Ring cleric retiring just after the time specified

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: retiring means going backwards, so the cleric's word is reversed

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman
due means fair or just, as in due reward

explanation.surface: Phone a vicar who has retired once his time is up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a telephone call or a wedding ring, but stands for O. REV backwards gives VER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overdue arrives late, after the time it was expected.

clue.text: Fussy eater abandoned pie and preserve

indicators.note: abandoned in the sense of wild and unrestrained, so the letters run riot

parts.note: to cure food is to preserve it, by salting or smoking

explanation.surface: Someone picky about food leaves a pie behind and keeps some jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' reads as left uneaten, but it is the anagram signal: PIE becomes EPI. 'Preserve' suggests jam, but here is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure has refined, discriminating taste in food and drink, which makes for a particular eater.

clue.text: Information contained in a lawyer's schedule

indicators.note: contained in means the information sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, an American lawyer
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Details found within an attorney's timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gen' is British informal for the facts on something; 'contained in' places it inside the lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list of items to be dealt with, a schedule for a meeting.

clue.text: Bunting possibly put up over obstruction in tiny stream

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the bird's word is read upwards

parts.note: a bunting is a kind of small bird
a let is an old word for a hindrance, still heard in 'without let or hindrance' and in tennis

explanation.surface: Flags strung up over a barrier across a little brook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunting' suggests festive flags but is the songbird; 'possibly' marks it as one example of a bird. BIRD upwards is DRIB.
explanation.definitionFit: A driblet is a small trickle or dribble of liquid, a very small flow.

clue.text: Noncommittal type maintaining boundaries

definitions.meaning: someone who avoids committing themselves, who sits on the fence
someone who plants and trims the hedges that mark field edges

explanation.walkthrough: 'Maintaining boundaries' sounds like personal boundaries, but here it is the literal work of keeping hedges.
explanation.definitionFit: One who hedges evades a direct answer; one who tends hedges keeps field edges in shape.

clue.text: Measure of cloth one wouldn't want in one's coffin?

definitions.meaning: an old unit for cloth of two and a quarter inches

definitions.text: one wouldn't want in one's coffin?
definitions.meaning: from the phrase 'another ... in one's coffin', something hastening ruin

explanation.walkthrough: A nail was an old unit for measuring cloth, a sixteenth of a yard.
explanation.definitionFit: The nail was a traditional measure for cloth; and a nail in the coffin is a hastener of one's end.

clue.text: In eclipse it's awfully black to go to vote

indicators.note: In says the letter for black goes inside the rearranged letters
awfully means badly, so these letters are made a mess of

parts.note: it, with the 's read as a joining 'is'
B is the pencil abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: During an eclipse it is terribly dark, so off to the polls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' scrambles the eclipse letters into PLEISCITE, and 'In' puts the black letter inside. 'Black' looks like the darkness of an eclipse.
explanation.definitionFit: A plebiscite is a direct vote by a whole electorate on a single question.

clue.text: Speculator without female escort

definitions.meaning: on the stock exchange, someone who applies for new shares to sell at a quick profit
a man attending without a woman partner

explanation.walkthrough: In stock-market slang a stag buys new share issues to sell them on at once.
explanation.definitionFit: In financial slang a stag is a quick-profit speculator; going stag means attending without a woman.

clue.text: Attest authenticity of token on bar

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the token follows the bar

parts.note: a counter is a bar where drinks or goods are served
a sign is a token or indication

explanation.surface: A token placed on a pub bar proves something is genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Token' and 'bar' both look like objects at a pub, but each supplies a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To countersign is to add a second signature confirming that a document is authentic.

clue.text: Convict taking drink without hesitation

indicators.note: without means the hesitation is removed from the drink

parts.note: lager is a drink, a light beer
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A prisoner downs a beer without a moment's pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convict' looks like a verb but is a noun: a lag is British slang for a prisoner, especially an old lag.
explanation.definitionFit: A lag is British slang for a convict, especially a long-term prisoner.

clue.text: Issue from work unit in Eastern state

indicators.note: in signals that the work unit is put inside the other pieces

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for Maine, a US state
the erg is a unit of work or energy

explanation.surface: Something emerging from a work unit in an eastern state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a noun but is the verb: come out. Maine as ME is the US postal code.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come out or issue forth from somewhere.

clue.text: Lover said "Farewell — another time" 22,882

indicators.note: said means the words are spoken, so the answer sounds like them

parts.note: farewell is adieu and another time is later, so adieu, later

explanation.surface: A sweetheart bidding goodbye with a promise to meet again.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing 22,882 is the puzzle's number picked up by the OCR, not part of the clue. 'Lover' is a fan or admirer, not a romantic partner.
explanation.definitionFit: An adulator lavishes praise and admiration, so is a lover in the sense of a devotee.
